controls.rule: Every contribution or moderation mutation is refused unless the user is logged in.
A user acting on behalf of an organization must be a member of it, and a user in several organizations must name one.
A conflict-of-interest statement counts as valid only for one year after it was filed, so every COI-gated moderation action is refused once it expires.
A new evidence item is refused if an identical submitted or accepted evidence item already exists.
A new evidence item is refused if its molecular profile does not exist or is deprecated.
A new evidence item must have a description of at least 50 characters.
Evidence items must satisfy type-specific field rules (significance, direction, disease, therapy, interaction type, non-deprecated terms) or they are invalid.
An evidence item is invalid if its source is retracted (Retraction Watch) or deprecated.
An optional comment attached to a new evidence item must be at least 10 characters.
On submission an evidence item gets a review due date 14 days ahead for Predictive evidence and 30 days ahead otherwise.
A daily job reassigns submitted evidence items whose review is past due to a different editor, resets the due date to 7 days ahead and increments the escalation count.
Automatic reviewer assignment never picks the submitter (or the excluded current assignee).
Automatic reviewer assignment considers only editors/admins with a valid conflict-of-interest statement, preferring the one with fewest open assignments.
An editor who already has 25 open (submitted) assignments is not assigned another evidence review.
Pulling the next item from the moderation queue endpoint requires sign-in, editor role and a valid COI statement.
The moderation queue orders submitted evidence items flagged first, then by earliest review due date, then oldest.
The next-item endpoint never hands an editor an evidence item they submitted themselves.
The next-item endpoint only hands out items that are unassigned or assigned to the requesting editor.
The GraphQL review_queue listing excludes flagged items and the requester's own submissions and orders by review due date.
Only users with at least editor role may moderate (accept, reject, revert) evidence items.
A user may not accept an evidence item they submitted (unless the policy exception K23 applies).
A submitter may reject their own evidence item without being an editor.
An admin with a valid COI may accept their own submitted evidence item once it has waited more than 180 days.
The acceptance policy requires an editor with a valid COI statement who is not the submitter.
Rejecting or reverting an evidence item requires a comment.
A comment must not be supplied when accepting an evidence item.
A moderation action is refused if the evidence item already has the requested status.
An evidence item cannot be accepted if its source is retracted or deprecated.

Accepting (or reverting) an evidence item saves with full model validation, so an item that is currently invalid (e.g. deprecated molecular profile/disease/therapy) cannot be accepted; rejection skips validation.
Rejecting an evidence item supersedes all of its open revisions.
Rejecting an evidence item moves active approvals of assertions that use it to requires_review.
Accepting a revision to evidence_level, significance, evidence_direction or molecular_profile_id of an accepted evidence item sends it back to submitted.
An accepted evidence item with open flags from at least 3 distinct users is set back to submitted.
A submitter may withdraw (status set to rejected) their own submitted evidence item if it is not linked to any assertion and not flagged.
Withdrawal is refused if the evidence item already has accepted revisions.
A rake task rejects (as the bot user) all submitted evidence items whose source is retracted.
The daily Retraction Watch import flags every evidence item whose source is newly marked as retracted (once per item).
When a source is no longer marked retracted, the bot's retraction flags on its evidence items are resolved automatically.
When a source is no longer marked retracted, its rejected evidence items are flagged for re-evaluation.
Revisions cannot be suggested to a rejected evidence item.
An assertion must cite at least one evidence item unless it is of Oncogenic type.
Assertions must satisfy type-specific field rules (significance, direction, disease, therapy, ACMG/ClinGen codes, AMP level, NCCN version).
An assertion submission or revision is refused if any cited evidence item is currently invalid.
An assertion cannot be accepted while any of its supporting evidence items is not accepted.
Only users with at least editor role may moderate assertions.
A user may not accept an assertion they submitted.
A submitter may reject their own assertion without being an editor.
Rejecting or reverting an assertion requires a comment.
A comment must not be supplied when accepting an assertion.
A moderation action is refused if the assertion already has the requested status.
Reverting an accepted assertion that has active organization approvals is refused unless the user may reopen decided items.
Admins, and editors with a valid COI who hold the reopen privilege, may reopen decided items.
Rejecting an assertion moves its active approvals to requires_review.
Changing the AMP level or significance of an accepted assertion moves its active approvals to requires_review.
Accepting revisions on an evidence item or assertion moves active approvals of the affected assertions to requires_review.
An accepted assertion with open flags from at least 3 distinct users is set back to submitted.
An assertion can be approved on behalf of an organization only if it is accepted.
A flagged assertion cannot be approved.
An assertion cannot be approved twice for the same organization while an active approval exists.
Approving or revoking an approval requires approval privileges for that organization.
Approving an assertion requires a valid COI statement.
Revoking an approval requires a comment of at least 10 characters and exactly one active or requires_review approval from the organization.
Flagging an entity with approvals moves its active approvals to requires_review.
Flags raised on accepted assertions with an active approval get high priority.
When the last open flag on an entity is resolved, approvals that this flag pushed to requires_review return to active.
A revision suggestion requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
The revised object must pass model validation before revisions are created.
A revision suggestion must change at least one field.
A suggestion whose every revision duplicates an existing open revision is refused (duplicates are reused, not recreated).
Accepting revisions requires at least editor role (unless K71 applies).
The submitter of a still-submitted evidence item or assertion may accept revisions to it without being an editor or having a COI.
Accepting revisions requires a valid COI statement.
A user may not accept their own suggested revision.
Only revisions in status new can be accepted or rejected.
Revisions accepted or rejected together must share one subject.
Revisions accepted together may not include two revisions of the same field.
An optional acceptance comment must be at least 10 characters.
Rejecting revisions requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
A revisor may reject their own revision without being an editor.
Rejecting someone else's revision requires at least editor role.
Rejecting someone else's revision requires a valid COI statement.
An accepted or rejected revision is final and its status cannot be changed.
Accepting a revision supersedes all other open revisions on the same field of the same subject.
A monthly job supersedes open revisions older than one year that have had no comment in the last 90 days.
Raising a flag requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
A user may not open a second flag on an entity where they already have an open flag.
Raising a flag marks the flagged entity as flagged.
A weekly job flags (as the bot) non-deprecated variants that share an Allele Registry ID with another variant.
Resolving a flag requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
Only open flags can be resolved.
The user who raised a flag may resolve it without being an editor.
A user may not resolve another user's flag raised against their own submission.
Resolving another user's flag requires at least editor role.
Resolving another user's flag requires a valid COI statement.
Admins may resolve any open flag, bypassing the own-submission and COI checks.
Editors in the CIViC Editorial Team organization may resolve bot-raised flags, bypassing the own-submission and COI checks.
A resolved flag must record the resolving user.
When no open flags remain on an entity, its flagged marker is cleared.
A comment body must be at least 10 characters.
A comment body may not exceed 20,000 characters.
Only the author may delete a comment, and an already deleted comment cannot be deleted again.
A source suggestion requires an existing source, a comment of at least 10 characters, existing non-deprecated molecular profile/therapies and consistent therapy interaction type.
A source suggestion must name a molecular profile or a disease.
A suggestion is refused if an open (new) suggestion already exists for the same source, molecular profile and disease.
On creation a source suggestion is assigned to the editor/admin (not the suggester) with fewest assigned suggestions.
An editor without a valid COI statement may not change a source suggestion's status.
Status changes are limited to new->curated/rejected and curated/rejected->new.
A suggestion cannot be marked curated unless its source has a submitted or accepted evidence item.
A curated or rejected source suggestion may be returned to new (requeued).
A weekly job rejects source suggestions left in status new for more than two years, bypassing validation.

notes: Uncertain or worth checking: (1) ModerateEvidenceItem#authorized?: if EvidenceItemPolicy#accept? fails, an editor who is not the submitter is still authorized by the editor check at line 66, so the COI requirement for accepting evidence (K24) is effectively not enforced; reverting an accepted evidence item needs only editor role (no reopen privilege check, unlike assertions). (2) ModerateEvidenceItem ready? line 28 references undefined new_stats (would raise NameError, still refuses). (3) Moderation::Withdrawal (K34-K35) and EvidenceReviewAssigner#assign! are not called from any mutation/controller; the assigner is only used by the escalation job, so no reviewer is assigned at submission. (4) K36 rake task is not in scheduled_tasks.yml (manual run). (5) Retraction importer resolve_eid_flags (K38) uses an undefined variable `text` at line 83, so that branch would fail at runtime. (6) Selection rules conflict: moderation_queue scope puts flagged items first (K16) while the review_queue resolver excludes flagged items (K19). (7) Disabled/dead code not coded as controls: auto-accept of trivial description revisions (accept_revisions.rb:59 returns false), old behaviour reverting accepted flaggables on flag resolution (resolve_flag.rb:32 'if false'), commented-out 'resolve flags before accepting' guard (moderate_evidence_item.rb:41), TODO auto-close old flags (flag.rb:16). (8) UpdateSourceSuggestionStatus allows any signed-in non-editor to change status (only editors are COI-checked). (9) Moderated#prevent_destroying_decided_records (moderated.rb:37) blocks hard deletion of accepted records; not coded since no review event. Deprecation mutations (variant/feature/MP, DeprecationValidator) guard against deprecating entities with submitted/accepted evidence or open revisions; treated as entity management, not review, and not coded. (10) Duplicate-check and validation rules for other suggest_*_revision mutations (features, variants, MPs) were consolidated into K66-K69.
